kilauea_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY DAILY UPDATE
kilauea_notices.message: HVO Kilauea ORANGE/WATCH - Glow, flames, and minor spattering over the past day; no additional eruptive activity. Kīlauea's summit remains at a high level of pressurization with changes in eruptive activity or location within the summit region possible.
kilauea_notices.detail: Summit Observations: The north, south, and west vents in Halemaʻumaʻu all showed strong glow and flames in overnight webcam imagery, with occasional gas jetting and spattering from the north vent. No sustained fountaining or overflows have been observed since the overflows on October 12. Summit tremor changed from a pattern of minor tremor bursts to constant tremor around 8 a.m. HST this morning. In the past 24 hours, there were 22 shallow earthquakes located across the summit region of Kīlauea, predominantly in the south caldera region. Summit tiltmeters have shown minor changes in tilt, with an overall slight deflationary trend over the past day. GPS stations on opposite sides of Halemaʻumaʻu (CRIM and UWEV) show a small increase in length since the end of September suggesting longer-term inflation of the summit magma reservoir. Updated interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) interferograms following the dike intrusion on September 30-October 1, show the intrusion has been slightly contracting since the evening of October 2. Minor intrusion-related motion was observed along many faults and cracks formed during the 2018 caldera collapse. There are no signs of significant deformation outside the caldera, including the south caldera region. During inter-episode pauses, the sulfur dioxide (SO2) emission rate from the summit typically varies between 1,000 and 5,000 tonnes per day. Plumes of volcanic gas are visible from the vents in day-time webcam views. Winds are currently forecast from the northeast through tomorrow. Rift Zone Observations: Rates of seismicity and ground deformation remain low in the East Rift Zone and Southwest Rift Zone. SO2 emissions from the East Rift Zone remain below the detection limit. No significant ground deformation was recorded in either rift zone. Analysis: Kīlauea had been erupting episodically between December 23, 2024, and August 25, 2026, from two vents (north and south) in Halema‘uma‘u at the summit. Lava fountaining episodes generally lasted for less than 12 hours and were separated by pauses of two or more weeks. Irregular patterns of ground deformation at Kīlauea summit since the most recent lava fountaining episode, number 54 on August 25, 2026, prevent forecast modeling for when the next fountaining episode can occur. Ground deformation patterns indicate the magma chamber beneath Halemaʻumaʻu is pressurized beyond the level typically seen before recent fountaining events. This pattern was disrupted by the dike intrusion on September 30-October 1 and since then summit tilt has increased slowly with interspersed periods of decreased or flat tilt. Intermittent spattering overnight indications that magma remains high in the established vent complex and produces visible gas jetting and spattering during drainback events. It is possible that another fountaining episode from the north-south vent complex could occur; however, intrusive activity underneath Kaluapele is also possible, or magma could exploit existing weak crack systems in the summit region to erupt passively (with little or no seismicity or deformation). HVO continues to closely monitor Kīlauea and is in contact with Hawai‘i Volcanoes National Park and the Hawai‘i County Civil Defense Agency about eruptive hazards. Kīlauea volcano alert level and aviation color code remain at WATCH/ORANGE and conditions could change rapidly. For further details, see the recent official notices listed below. mauna_loa_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY MONTHLY UPDATE
mauna_loa_notices.message: HVO Mauna Loa GREEN/NORMAL - Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues.
mauna_loa_notices.detail: Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks. No earthquakes occurred directly beneath Mokuʻāweoweo. Data from Global Positioning System (GPS) instruments on Mauna Loa showed slight inflation across the summit region in the past month. Oscillations between contraction and inflation patterns during non-eruptive periods are normal, but inflation has been the dominant trend since the 2022 eruption, consistent with magma refilling the summit reservoir system. Gas and temperature data from a station on Mauna Loa's Southwest Rift Zone indicate these values are at background levels, with little change relative to previous months. HVO continues to closely monitor Mauna Loa and will issue another update in one month, or earlier, should conditions change significantly.
